newsitem.title: USA: Texas May sales tax rebates up $19.7 mln from 1996.
newsitem.headline: Texas May sales tax rebates up $19.7 mln from 1996.

text.p: The Texas state comptroller Friday delivered a total of $216.5 million in monthly sales tax payments to 1,086 Texas cities and 117 counties.

"The Texas economy continues its slow, steady expansion and May sales tax rebates to Texas cities and counties are $19.7 million higher than those for May 1996," Texas Comptroller John Sharp said in a release. "Year-to-date, Texas allocations are running 5.6 percent ahead of the first five months of last year."

Texas cities received sales tax rebates totaling $199.3 million, 9.9 percent higher than last May's payments of $181.3 million. Sharp delivered rebates of $17.1 million to Texas counties, 11.1 percent more than allocations of $15.4 million to counties in May 1996. City transit and special purpose districts received a combined $7.7 million in May rebates.

This month's sales tax rebates include local sales taxes collected on March sales by businesses filing monthly returns and reporting to the comptroller in April, as well as those businesses filing quarterly returns for January, February and March.
